stimulus.body: A 2015 study of 2400 high-school students in the American South reported that 51% saw shared institutions as necessary for order, while 9% saw them mainly as tools of one group.

questions.stem: Which definition matches the 2015 South social stability result?

options.text: a view that social institutions work together to maintain stability and meet societal needs
a view that society is divided by inequality and struggles over power
options.misconception: reads every institution as a site of cooperation

options.text: a view centered on small-scale interaction and shared meanings
options.misconception: reduces institutions to face-to-face gestures

options.text: the idea that reality is built through collective definitions
options.misconception: confuses the making of meaning with an institution's function

questions.explanation: A view that social institutions work together to maintain stability and meet societal needs. The 2015 finding about social stability is an instance of this idea, not of the alternatives, which point to different processes.
questions.hint: Look past the numbers to the relationship they describe.

stimulus.body: A 2019 study of 3000 working mothers in the American South reported that 65% saw shared institutions as necessary for order, while 15% saw them mainly as tools of one group.

questions.stem: Explain the 2019 South finding about social stability.

answer.exemplar: A 2019 study of 3000 working mothers in the American South reported that 65% saw shared institutions as necessary for order, while 15% saw them mainly as tools of one group. This illustrates structural functionalism: a view that social institutions work together to maintain stability and meet societal needs. A careful reading links the group-level pattern to the wider social structure rather than to any single person, and it distinguishes this idea from competing accounts that locate the cause elsewhere.

questions.explanation: The finding illustrates structural functionalism: a view that social institutions work together to maintain stability and meet societal needs. The 65 percent versus 15 percent split in the American South shows why this reading fits better than the alternatives.
questions.hint: Ask what would have to be true for both figures to hold.
